house_rules: No-DoS law (organ doctrine, from Heyes' black-box detection research): every server-side probe below is a HARMLESS property write whose only footprint is an observable response difference - crash-style probes (polluting toString/valueOf on hot paths) are forbidden.
The hunting order is source -> gadget -> sink: a source alone is an informational FACT; the finding is the chain.
Payloads are canonical forms from the public record, attributed per entry.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a probe that failed for a listed reason leaves the merge path untested, not safe.

source.title: Server-side prototype pollution: Black-box detection without the DoS (JSON-based techniques)

prerequisites: framework whose error/status path consults object properties (Express-adjacent stacks)
entries.probe: pollute {"__proto__":{"status":599}} (harmless, non-standard code) then trigger ANY normal request
entries.oracle: subsequent responses carry status 599 (or the polluted value in the response line) - the framework read Object.prototype.status as its default; reverse the probe immediately (status 200) to clean up
failure_modes: framework pins status explicitly on every path - default never consulted
reverse-cleanup probe mandatory: leave the process CLEAN (organ's operator-respect rule), never 500-class values on shared infra
